findings.title: Fraud Check Endpoint Uses Malformed Double-Path
findings.description: The fraud check endpoint call uses path '/fraud/fraud/check' which creates a malformed URL with double 'fraud' segments. This violates REST API conventions and creates technical debt.
findings.evidence:
Code at line 490: `const response = await apiCall(`${CONFIG.API_BASE_URL}/fraud/fraud/check`, {`

Root cause: Server.js registers transactions router at '/api/fraud' (server.js:60), and transactions router defines endpoint as '/fraud/check' (transactions.js:116), creating path '/api/fraud' + '/fraud/check' = '/api/fraud/fraud/check'
findings.consequence: API path inconsistency, maintenance confusion, technical debt. While the system may work functionally, this violates REST conventions and will cause issues during API evolution and documentation.
findings.requiredFix:
Option A (Recommended):
1. Change backend/routes/transactions.js line 116 from `router.post('/fraud/check', ...)` to `router.post('/check', ...)`
2. Change frontend/js/face-verification.js line 490 from `${CONFIG.API_BASE_URL}/fraud/fraud/check` to `${CONFIG.API_BASE_URL}/fraud/check`

This creates the correct path: /api/fraud + /check = /api/fraud/check
